claims.claim: Equinix identity/tradability is validated as NASDAQ:EQIX (CIK 0001101239); current cumulative evidence resolves to two independent SEC filing origins, with six duplicate references collapsed by the packet reconciler.

Q2 2026 operating evidence is primary-source current for T0 underwriting; issuer IR independently exposes the same quarter's filing/results surfaces, while current valuation is separately sourced from a market-data aggregator and is treated as non-primary valuation evidence only.

risks.risk: Issuer evidence is not independent corroboration of issuer claims; valuation source is independent but non-canonical market evidence.

unknowns.unknown: Current evidence does not isolate AI-specific incremental ROIC from the broader portfolio.

claims.claim: Q2 2026 MRR grew 11% year over year, annualized gross bookings grew 23%, backlog reached a record, AFFO/share grew 18% normalized constant-currency, and management raised 2026 revenue growth guidance to 11-12% and AFFO/share growth to 10-12%.

Equinix operates 282 data centers across 77 metros and 36 countries with more than 10,500 customers and 522,000 interconnections; roughly 78% cabinet utilization and rising power density support network/platform scarcity while power/cooling delivery remains a material execution constraint.

At roughly $104.3B market capitalization and about $1,057/share on September 21, 2026 after a strong year-to-date rerating, valuation evidence supports a demanding rather than cheap anchor despite strong operating momentum.

risks.risk: Power/cooling availability and capital intensity can delay monetization of otherwise strong demand.
Current valuation embeds substantial growth expectations and reduces downside-adjusted headroom.

unknowns.unknown: AI-specific incremental return on capital is not separately disclosed.
Current source set does not establish exceptional supplier redundancy for utility and cooling constraints.

thesisQuality.basis: Record backlog, 23% bookings growth, 11% MRR growth and dense interconnection footprint support durable demand/value capture; capital intensity prevents exceptional-band treatment.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Q2 MRR +11% YoY, AFFO/share +18% normalized constant-currency and raised 2026 guidance support the strong anchor; power/capacity execution remains a constraint.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: September 21 market cap about $104.3B and share price about $1,057 after a strong rerating indicate demanding valuation relative to even double-digit growth; evidence supports weak-to-mixed headroom, not a cheap asymmetry.

catalystScore.basis: Raised 2026 guidance, record backlog and management's 2029 growth outlook provide multiple source-supported operating catalysts, though timing depends on capacity delivery.

governancePower.basis: Current management has delivered raised guidance and strong AFFO/share growth with transparent SEC/IR reporting; evidence supports strong execution but does not establish exceptional long-duration stewardship.

alignment2036.basis: Global colocation/interconnection infrastructure directly serves durable cloud, networking and AI-density needs across 77 metros; power-density growth reinforces long-duration strategic relevance.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: More than 10,500 customers, 522,000 interconnections, 282 data centers and 77 metros create multiple independent customer/geographic demand engines using the same platform.

bottleneckControl.basis: High utilization, dense interconnection and constrained power/cooling capacity support control of scarce, difficult-to-replicate digital-infrastructure locations; utilities remain an external dependency.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Global diversification and exposure to AI, cloud and networking provide several demand paths, offset by common dependence on power/cooling and capital delivery.

substitutionResilience.basis: Large interconnection ecosystem and installed global footprint create qualification/network switching friction, while alternative architectures/locations remain credible substitutes for incremental workloads.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Geographic breadth provides some resilience, but filings identify power/cooling/capacity delivery as meaningful dependencies and current evidence does not demonstrate exceptional redundancy.

pricingPower.basis: Double-digit recurring revenue growth alongside AFFO/share expansion and high utilization supports demonstrated economic capture, but evidence does not isolate pure price realization from volume/mix.

riskEvidence.basis: Material risks are capital intensity, constrained power/cooling delivery and a demanding current valuation; demand evidence remains strong, so risk is meaningful but not thesis-breaking.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Identity and operating claims are grounded in current SEC filings and issuer results; current valuation has an independent market source. Confidence is reduced for undisclosed AI-specific economics and supplier redundancy.

scoreRecord.thesis: Equinix combines a globally distributed colocation footprint with a dense interconnection ecosystem that can capture durable AI/cloud/networking demand, while scarce power-ready capacity increases both strategic value and execution dependence.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: Power/cooling and capital-delivery constraints can delay monetization while a demanding valuation leaves less room for execution misses.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Conversion of record backlog and raised 2026 guidance into sustained recurring-revenue and AFFO/share growth as new capacity is energized.

scoreBreakdown.note: earthScore is the methodology-weighted component base; risk and confidence are separately recorded for downstream locked gate/penalty treatment.
